clue.text: Affectionate address from musical great

definitions.meaning: in Welsh usage '...' is a term of endearment, like 'dear' or 'love'
Johann Sebastian, the German Baroque composer

explanation.walkthrough: The Welsh endearment is everyday British knowledge rather than crossword lore: Welsh speakers call someone 'bach', roughly 'my dear'.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a Welsh endearment meaning little one; the other is the surname of the celebrated Baroque composer.

clue.text: To keep in shape without extremes of exertion is an advantage

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the first piece wraps around the second

parts.note: to be fit is to keep in shape

indicators.note: extremes of picks out the first and last letters of exertion

explanation.surface: Staying fit without pushing to the limit is a good thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A benefit is a gain or helpful factor, the same thing as an advantage.

clue.text: Film-makers appeared with Japanese dish

parts.note: came means turned up or appeared
ramen is a Japanese noodle soup

explanation.surface: Movie people turned up with a bowl of Japanese noodles.
explanation.definitionFit: The camera operators on a shoot are among those who make films.

clue.text: Band's number one songs heard after operatic work

indicators.note: after puts the songs piece behind the operatic work in the answer

parts.note: Wagner's Ring cycle is known simply as the Ring

indicators.note: heard says the word for songs is to be taken by its sound

explanation.surface: A music review: a group's chart-topping songs following on from an opera.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief of a gang or band, especially of troublemakers, is its instigator and head.

clue.text: Man, for example, I defame without hesitation

indicators.note: without means the hesitation sound is removed

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone confessing they malign a man without pausing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person; it is the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an example of a piece of land surrounded by sea.

clue.text: Note an insult that was illuminating for Fanny

parts.note: a slight is a snub or insult

explanation.surface: A remark and a snub that enlightened a woman called Fanny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fanny by Gaslight' is a 1940 Michael Sadleir novel, filmed in 1944: so the lamp lit Fanny.
explanation.definitionFit: Gas lamps lit the scenes of Fanny's story, so the lighting is literally what illuminated her.

clue.text: For instance, settled on heresy as radical policy

parts.note: eg abbreviates exempli gratia, for instance
alit means landed or settled on something
Arianism was an early Christian heresy denying Christ's full divinity

explanation.surface: An example of a heretical idea that took hold as an extreme political line.
explanation.definitionFit: Egalitarianism, the belief in equality for all, is a radical political creed.

clue.text: Skilful packaging for fifty crockery pieces

indicators.note: packaging for means wrapping round the next piece

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Careful wrapping of fifty plates and cups.
explanation.definitionFit: Delft is the blue-and-white tin-glazed pottery made in the Dutch town of that name.

clue.text: Withdrew part of army, exhausted

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army

explanation.surface: A worn-out army unit pulled back.
explanation.definitionFit: Retired means went away or pulled back, a synonym of withdrew.

clue.text: A leader of mob in disorderly direct action is this?

definitions.text: A leader of mob in disorderly direct action is this?

indicators.note: in places the leader's letter within the jumbled phrase
disorderly means the letters of direct action are thrown into disarray
leader of picks the first letter of mob

explanation.surface: A mob ringleader in a riot of direct action: is this against democracy?
explanation.walkthrough: A semi-&lit: read whole, the clue asks whether a mob-led riot is itself against democracy, so the wordplay doubles as the description.
explanation.definitionFit: Mob rule through direct action bypasses elected government, which is opposed to democracy.

clue.text: Minor crash on main line

indicators.note: a crash smashes the words on and main into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A small accident on the main railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominal sum or role is token, slight, negligible: so minor in size or importance.

clue.text: Bulb planted in Irish allotment

indicators.note: planted in means set within the run of letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A gardener putting a bulb into the soil of an allotment in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: An allotment is a small rented plot for growing vegetables, common in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallot is a small onion-like vegetable that grows from a bulb.

clue.text: Senior politician, a churchman from Rome?

definitions.meaning: the cabinet member in charge of a country's dealings abroad
a clergyman (minister) who comes from another country, Italy say, is literally a minister who is foreign

explanation.definitionFit: The government post handling external affairs; whimsically, a priest who is not a native is an overseas cleric.

clue.text: Mainly medium or moderate

indicators.note: mainly means most of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: tempera is a painting medium of pigment mixed with egg

explanation.surface: Advice to be largely middle of the road or restrained.
explanation.definitionFit: To temper something is to tone it down or soften it, which is a verb sense of moderate.

clue.text: Foolhardy interrupting the Duke, severely punished

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into the middle of the other piece

explanation.surface: Someone reckless barges in on a duke and gets a beating for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrashed means beaten hard, a severe physical punishment.

clue.text: Longing to include boss, initially, one that's a great example

indicators.note: to include means the longing wraps round the other letters

parts.note: hunger means a longing or craving
MD, the initials of managing director, the boss of a company
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A yearning to bring in the boss's initials, an outstanding instance.
explanation.definitionFit: A humdinger is an informal word for something remarkable or excellent of its kind.

clue.text: I'd got upset by ally, so dreadfully untrustworthy

indicators.note: upset means the letters are knocked over and rearranged
dreadfully adds a second signal that the letters are in a mess

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe giving no letter

explanation.surface: Someone distressed by a friend who proves badly unreliable.
explanation.definitionFit: Disloyal means failing to keep faith, so not to be trusted.

clue.text: Geniality from British cricket side I spotted in familiar surroundings

parts.note: the on side is the leg side of a cricket field

indicators.note: spotted in places the letter inside the next piece

parts.note: home is the place one knows best

explanation.surface: A friendly mood in a British cricket team that I noticed at a home ground.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is split into the off side and the on (leg) side.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonhomie is cheerful friendliness, a close synonym of good-natured warmth.

clue.text: Assassin beheaded poet

indicators.note: beheaded means the first letter of the word is cut off

explanation.surface: A killer who decapitated a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: A hired killer is a professional murderer, the same as an assassin.

clue.text: Chivalrous in speech, as stars appear

indicators.note: in speech says the word for chivalrous is to be taken by its sound

parts.note: knightly means chivalrous, like a knight

explanation.surface: Gallant words spoken as stars come out.
explanation.definitionFit: Stars come out every night, so the adverb for each evening describes their appearance.

clue.text: Religious type putting end to daylight robbery

indicators.note: end to picks the last letter of daylight

explanation.surface: A pious person stops a robbery in broad daylight.
explanation.definitionFit: A theist believes in God, so is a religious person.

clue.text: More recent material for writer found in parliament's unorthodox reasoning

indicators.note: found in means placed inside the next piece

parts.note: ink is what a writer uses

explanation.surface: Newer writing supplies discovered in parliament reflect off-beat thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase coined by Edward de Bono means solving problems by an indirect, creative approach.

clue.text: Warm around South, precisely

indicators.note: around means the phrase for precisely goes round the next letter

explanation.surface: Heat exactly around the south.
explanation.definitionFit: To toast bread or one's toes by a fire is to warm it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Good and quick protecting pound — that's awful

indicators.note: protecting means wrapped round the next piece

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound sterling, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone sound and quick who guards the pound: a bad outcome after all.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghastly means horrible or dreadful, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Understanding 4 weird things

parts.note: the answer to 4 Down is island, abbreviated I

indicators.note: weird signals that the letters of things are set out oddly

explanation.surface: Grasping some strange items.
explanation.walkthrough: 4 refers to 4 Down, whose answer (an isle like Man) is shortened to its usual abbreviation I; 'weird' turns THINGS into NSIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Insight is penetrating comprehension, a synonym of understanding.

clue.text: Express in sections jointed together

definitions.meaning: a verb: to put clearly into words
an adjective: made of segments connected by joints, as an insect's body

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to utter clearly; as an adjective it describes segmented, hinged bodies or vehicles.

clue.text: Suffer peripheral damage in battle

definitions.meaning: cloth that wears at the edges

explanation.definitionFit: Fabric unravelling at its edges is one sense; the other is a noisy fight or brawl.
